subject: Formative Measurement Model unidentified and baseline model failed

messages.author: b38f344d5cde2da0
messages.subject: Formative Measurement Model unidentified and baseline model failed
parts:
Dear Sir/ Madam,

Good day to you! I have one concern regarding the model syntax and problem in model identification.

This is the syntax I have used.

model <- ' 
safety <~ 1*q1 + q2 + q3 + q8 + q9 + q10
efficiency <~ 1*q12 + q13 + q14 + q16 + q17 + q19
maintenance <~ 1*q20 + q21 + q22 + q23 + q24
safety ~ efficiency
efficiency ~ maintenance
maintenance ~ safety
'

The path diagram is reflective type but I would like to get it in formative model.

Using the syntax above, I have got no proper result and warnings like this.

Could you please kindly help me with some suggestions?
Thank you in advance.

Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING: all observed variables are exogenous; model may not be identified
2: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.
3: In lavaan::lavaan(model = three.model, data = busmdf, model.type = "cfa",  :
  lavaan WARNING: estimation of the baseline model failed.

messages.author: 5c634386b8a5a1ba
messages.subject: Re: Formative Measurement Model unidentified and baseline model failed
parts:
Hy Eaindray,

you use an arrow to specify the latent variables. However, only the model is specified with an arrow.

Here is an overview of the functions:

=~      measured by - latent variable definition
~        regression formulas = regression
~~      (co)variance formulas = correlation

Sandra.

messages.author: 5c634386b8a5a1ba
messages.subject: Re: Formative Measurement Model unidentified and baseline model failed
parts:
Dear Eaindray,

I think a notation like this <~ dosn't exist.

You have only to change your syntax from this notation <~ to this =~ and from this ~ to this ~~.
Maybe you want to add the variance and not only the covariance of your model (e.g. safety  ~~ safety).

Regards,
Sandra.

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: Formative Measurement Model unidentified and baseline model failed
parts:
Actually the "<~" operator exists: https://groups.google.com/forum/m/#!searchin/lavaan/Formative/lavaan/hnMCckaARoo
However, a formative measurement model can also be created without this operator. I think it is important to understand that a formative measurement with lavaan is not the same as with PLS.

messages.subject: Re: Formative Measurement Model unidentified and baseline model failed
parts:
If you want to create three correlated composites, you need a different package. If you like the lavaan syntax for model specification, consider the new cSEM package, which accepts lavaan syntax for specifying its models:
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/cSEM/vignettes/cSEM.html  
--Ed Rigdon
